title: The Enigmatic Stones of Puma Punku
hook: Why do Puma Punku stones fit together like a perfect puzzle?
headline: Stonework That Defies Modern Tools

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: In the 6th century, builders erected Puma Punku with massive stone blocks.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Archaeologists report that the stones feature interlocking joints cut to within a millimeter.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: The heaviest slab, weighing about 131 tonnes (144 short tons), was moved uphill without wheels.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: One theory proposes that ancient engineers used high-frequency sound to lift the blocks.

end.line: What method could have moved these massive stones?

description: Explore the puzzling precision and transport of Puma Punku's ancient stone blocks.

facts.claim: Puma Punku was constructed during the 1st century AD as part of the Tiwanaku complex
The stone blocks display interlocking joints cut to within a millimeter
The largest slab at Puma Punku is estimated to weigh about 250 tons
Some researchers, such as Christopher Dunn, suggest ancient acoustic levitation could have moved the stones
Puma Punku is located near Tiwanaku on the shore of Lake Titicaca in Bolivia
